analysis.investment_thesis: Cera Sanitaryware is a decent business with ROCE of ~22%, but at an EV of ~INR 6,923 Cr against EBIT of only INR 302 Cr, the earnings yield is a meager ~4.4% — far below the Magic Formula's 12% threshold. The stock is simply too expensive to buy with a margin of safety.
key_strengths: Virtually debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.04) with strong reserves of INR 1,347 Cr
Sustained ROCE of 22.4% and gross margins of ~51% indicate a branded product moat in sanitaryware
Net profit CAGR of 13% over 9 years — earnings compounding faster than revenue
key_risks: Revenue nearly flat — FY2024: INR 1,879 Cr → FY2025: INR 1,926 Cr (+2.5%) — growth stalling badly
EBITDA actually declined in FY2025 (INR 305 Cr vs INR 325 Cr), yet the stock trades at EV/EBITDA of 22x
Operating margin of only 8.27% despite 51% gross margins reveals heavy distribution/trade spend — structurally thin
red_flags: Other income of INR 57 Cr (2025) = ~23% of operating profit — earnings quality inflated by non-operating items
OCF of INR 122 Cr in FY2025 vs net profit of INR 249 Cr — major divergence, only 49% FCF conversion this year
Earnings yield of ~4.4% (EBIT INR 302 Cr / EV INR 6,923 Cr) fails Magic Formula minimum threshold of 12%
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: EBIT = INR 302 Cr (FY2025 operating income), EV = Market Cap INR 6,866 Cr + Debt INR 67 Cr − Cash INR 10 Cr = INR 6,923 Cr. Earnings Yield = 302/6,923 = **4.4%** — catastrophically low, less than a third of Greenblatt's 12% minimum. ROCE of 22.4% clears the hurdle on the quality side, but a good business at a bad price is still a bad investment. The Magic Formula demands BOTH metrics to be high; Cera only passes one.

The business fundamentals are softening, not strengthening. Revenue grew a mere 2.5% in FY2025, EBITDA contracted by INR 20 Cr YoY, and free cash flow collapsed to INR 94 Cr (vs INR 174 Cr in FY2024) — yet the market continues to price this at 27.8x P/E and 22x EV/EBITDA. The heavy reliance on other income (INR 57 Cr) to prop up reported earnings, combined with poor OCF-to-profit conversion, makes the quality of earnings suspect. At current valuations, the risk/reward is deeply unfavorable on a Magic Formula basis.
